content: If someone experiences severe symptoms such as losing consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to take it as soon as possible according to the prescribed schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. Common side effects may include stomach upset or mouth sores. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States or Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using rolapitant, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Rolapitant can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. This effect may persist for four weeks or longer after your dose of rolapitant. Other medications may also influence the removal of rolapitant from your body, which could impact its effectiveness. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, the poison control center can be reached at 1-800-222-1222. To store this medication, keep it at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
